pros: Generous 17 dedicated climbing days at altitude
Fixed ropes provided for glacier sections (45-50 degree slopes)
Three high camps on mini-summits with 360-degree panoramic views
Good training objective for future 8,000m peaks
Small group sizes; operator established since 1997
cons: Graded AD; requires prior 6,000m peak experience
Long 17-18 day commitment at high altitude
Cold, unpredictable weather and technical glacier travel
Possible flight cancellation/weather delays
verdict: A 30-day AD-grade climbing expedition with a long 17-day summit window; thorough and well-suited as a stepping stone toward 8,000m peaks.
excludes: International airfare, visa fees, personal insurance, tips, sleeping bag, services beyond base camp, and single-room supplements.

pros: Described as best 'training station' for K2 or Everest
Stated high success rate of over 80%
High-altitude porter (HAP) support and fixed ropes included
360-degree summit views of Nanga Parbat, K2, Broad Peak
Non-technical AD-grade route with minimal objective hazards
cons: Snow slopes 30-45 degrees; fixed ropes needed on steep sections
Graded AD and explicitly 'not a trekking peak'
High physical endurance demands on the summit ridge
Glacier navigation complexity

excludes: International flights, visas, personal insurance, climbing gear, excess baggage, emergency evacuation, and gratuities.

pros: Entry-level 7000m peak with minimal objective danger and few avalanche threats
1:3 guide ratio plus 1:1 local high-altitude porter
16 weeks of structured training program included
Emergency supplemental oxygen and satellite comms at base camp
Small teams (max 10) and all-inclusive pricing
cons: Long 700-800m vertical summit-day ridge ascent

Weather windows critical; 28-day commitment
Deposit non-refundable for natural-phenomenon delays
verdict: A 28-day, well-supported entry-level 7,000m expedition (USD 7,950) with strong guide ratios, included training and emergency oxygen, ideal for first-time high-altitude climbers.
excludes: Visas, travel insurance, international flights, summit bonus ($500+/member), evacuation costs, bottled drinks/laundry/phone, and natural-disaster cancellations.
